examples.en: This year every fruit tree is loaded with fruit.
I planted three fruit trees in the yard.
Fruit trees bloom in spring.
Bugs got on the fruit trees, so I sprayed them.
My grandfather's farm has a lot of fruit trees.

examples.ko: 과일나무 사이로 작은 길이 나 있어요.
examples.en: A small path runs between the fruit trees.

explain: 나무를 셀 때는 '그루'를 써서 '한 그루, 두 그루'라고 해요. 사과나무, 배나무처럼 과일 이름 뒤에 '나무'를 붙이는 말도 많아요.

phrases.en: There is one fruit tree in the yard.
phrases.nuance_ko: 나무를 셀 때 '그루'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Uses 그루 to count trees.

phrases.en: Apples grew on the apple tree.
phrases.nuance_ko: 과일 이름 뒤에 '나무'를 붙이면 구체적인 나무 이름이 돼요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 나무 after a fruit name gives a specific tree name.

phrases.en: My grandfather grows fruit trees in the countryside.
phrases.nuance_ko: 나무를 심고 가꾼다는 뜻으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means planting and taking care of trees.

explain_en: Trees are counted with '그루', as in '한 그루, 두 그루'. Many specific trees are formed by adding '나무' to the fruit name, like 사과나무 and 배나무.

examples.en: The snowflakes stuck coldly to my face.
Big snowflakes are falling from the sky.
The child caught a snowflake on his tongue.
Every single snowflake has a different shape.
Snowflakes are fluttering down outside the window.
A snowflake lightly landed on my glove.

explain: '송이'는 꽃이나 포도, 눈처럼 덩어리로 모인 것을 세는 말이에요. 눈이 '내리다', '날리다'라고 하고, 크고 포슬포슬한 눈은 '함박눈'이라고 해요. 말할 때는 '눈'이라고만 해도 충분하고 눈송이는 하나하나를 말할 때 써요.

phrases.en: Big snowflakes are falling outside the window.
phrases.nuance_ko: 눈송이의 크기를 말할 때 형용사를 앞에 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put an adjective in front to describe the flake's size.

phrases.en: Snowflakes fell quietly all night.
phrases.nuance_ko: 눈이 내리는 모습을 하나하나 그릴 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to picture snow falling flake by flake.

phrases.en: Big fluffy snow came down this morning.
phrases.nuance_ko: 크고 포슬포슬한 눈이 많이 올 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when big, fluffy snow comes down heavily.

explain_en: '송이' is a counter for things that come in clusters, like flowers, grapes and snow. Snow 'falls' (내리다) or 'drifts' (날리다), and big fluffy snow is '함박눈'. In speech '눈' alone is enough, and 눈송이 is used when talking about individual flakes.

examples.en: The weather in the mountains changes very quickly.
Our city keeps changing.

examples.ko: 사람의 생각은 시간이 지나면 변화하기도 해요.
examples.en: People's thinking can change over time.
Korean food culture has changed a lot.
We have to live in step with a changing world.
If the climate changes, farming is affected too.

explain: '변하다'보다 딱딱해서 글이나 뉴스에 잘 나와요. 말할 때는 '날씨가 변해요', '많이 달라졌어요'가 훨씬 자연스러워요. 명사 '변화'는 '변화가 생기다'처럼 자주 써요. 사람의 모습이 눈에 띄게 달라질 때는 '달라지다'를 써요.

phrases.en: The weather in the mountains changes often.
phrases.nuance_ko: '변화하다'보다 쉬워서 말할 때 더 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: Easier than 변화하다 and more natural in speech.

phrases.en: Our city has changed a lot.
phrases.nuance_ko: 전과 다른 모습이 눈에 띄게 될 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when something becomes noticeably different from before.

phrases.en: Recently there has been a change in my life.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 '변화'와 함께 새로운 달라짐이 생겼다고 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Uses the noun 변화 to say a new change has appeared.

explain_en: It is stiffer than '변하다' and appears in writing and news. In speech '날씨가 변해요' or '많이 달라졌어요' sounds more natural. The noun is common in '변화가 생기다' (a change occurs). For a person who looks or acts noticeably different, use '달라지다'.

dis.h: undergo change; more formal, often gradual

p.n: 변하다 is plainer and more everyday; 변화하다 suggests a larger, gradual development.

examples.ko: 이 회사는 일 년 사이클로 제품을 새로 내요.
examples.en: This company releases new products on a one-year cycle.
The cycle of new products coming out keeps getting shorter.

examples.ko: 동생은 사이클 선수가 되고 싶어 해요.
examples.en: My younger sibling wants to become a cycling athlete.
When the wash cycle ends, the washing machine stops.
The moon's cycle is about a month.
On weekends I go cycling along the Han River.

explain: '사이클'과 '주기'는 서로 바꿔 쓸 수 있는 경우가 많아요. '생활 사이클', '제품 사이클'처럼 앞에 말을 붙여요. 자전거 경기를 가리킬 때도 쓰는데, 자전거 타기는 보통 '자전거를 타다'라고 말해요.

phrases.en: My daily routine has changed a lot lately.
phrases.nuance_ko: 잠, 식사, 일 같은 하루 생활이 반복되는 흐름을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the repeating flow of daily life such as sleep, meals and work.

phrases.en: The cycle for new products is short.
phrases.nuance_ko: '사이클'과 바꿔 쓸 수 있고, 글이나 설명에서 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Interchangeable with 사이클, and a bit more common in writing and explanations.

phrases.en: I watched a cycling race on TV yesterday.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자전거로 겨루는 운동 경기를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for a sports competition on bicycles.

explain_en: '사이클' and '주기' can often replace each other. A word goes in front, as in '생활 사이클' and '제품 사이클'. It can also mean the cycling sport, but riding a bike is usually said '자전거를 타다'.

examples.ko: 가을이 되면 은행나무 잎이 노랗게 변해요.
examples.en: In autumn the leaves of the ginkgo tree turn yellow.
Let's meet under the ginkgo tree in front of the school.

examples.ko: 은행나무가 길 양쪽에 쭉 서 있어요.
examples.en: Ginkgo trees line both sides of the road.
The ginkgo tree lives for a very long time.
Ginkgo nuts fell from the tree and it smells.
I took pictures while walking along the ginkgo-lined road.

explain: '은행'은 열매 이름이고 '나무'를 붙이면 그 열매가 열리는 나무 이름이 돼요. 돈을 맡기는 곳 '은행'과 소리는 같지만 다른 말이에요. 노란 잎이 예뻐서 가을 풍경에 나와요.

phrases.en: Lots of ginkgo leaves have fallen on the ground.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가을 풍경을 말할 때 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common phrase when describing autumn scenery.

phrases.en: I walked along the ginkgo tree road in autumn.
phrases.nuance_ko: 은행나무가 줄지어 서 있는 길을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to a road lined with ginkgo trees.

phrases.example: 집 앞에 은행나무 한 그루가 있어요.
phrases.en: There is one ginkgo tree in front of my house.
phrases.nuance_ko: 나무를 셀 때는 '그루'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Trees are counted with the counter 그루.

explain_en: '은행' is the name of the nut, and adding '나무' makes the name of the tree. It sounds the same as '은행', the place where you keep money, but it is a different word. Its yellow leaves are pretty and appear in autumn scenery.

en: to be adapted; to be adjusted

examples.en: I'm not used to the new school yet.

examples.ko: 한 달 지나니까 매운 음식에 적응되고 있어요.
examples.en: After a month, I'm getting used to spicy food.
It was hard at first, but now I've adjusted.

examples.ko: 이사 온 동네가 슬슬 적응되는 것 같아요.
examples.en: I think I'm slowly getting used to the new neighborhood.

examples.ko: 야간 근무에 적응되면 훨씬 편해질 거예요.
examples.en: Once you get used to night shifts, it gets much easier.

examples.ko: 시차 때문에 힘들었지만 금방 적응되어서 다행이에요.
examples.en: Jet lag was tough, but I'm glad I adjusted quickly.

explain: '적응하다'는 내가 맞추려고 노력하는 느낌이고, '적응되다'는 어느새 익숙해져서 자연스러워진 상태예요. 보통 '-에 적응되다'로 써요. '익숙해지다'로 바꿔 말해도 비슷해요.

phrases.en: I am getting used to the house I moved into.
phrases.nuance_ko: '적응되다'와 비슷하고, 더 쉽고 일상적인 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to 적응되다, but easier and more everyday.

phrases.en: I adapted to the new company quickly.
phrases.nuance_ko: 내가 맞추려고 노력하는 느낌이 더 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Carries more of a feeling that I am making an effort to adjust.

phrases.example: 시차 때문에 아직 적응이 안 돼요.
phrases.en: Because of jet lag, I still cannot adjust.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아직 익숙하지 않다고 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Commonly used to say you are not used to it yet.

explain_en: '적응하다' feels like you are making an effort to fit in, while '적응되다' describes having become used to it without noticing. It's used as '-에 적응되다'. '익숙해지다' is a similar alternative.

en: to proceed; to be carried out; to go on (of an event)

examples.en: The meeting is going well as planned.
The road construction is moving very slowly.
The event was held starting at two in the afternoon.
If the class is conducted in English, it's hard to understand.
I am glad everything went smoothly.
Tomorrow's interview will be held online.

explain: '진행하다'는 사람이 이끌고, '진행되다'는 일이 정해진 절차대로 흘러가는 것이에요. 회의·행사·공사·수업·인터뷰처럼 순서가 있는 일에 써요. '잘 진행되다', '순조롭게 진행되다'가 자주 나오는 짝이에요.

phrases.en: The event went smoothly.
phrases.nuance_ko: 문제 없이 잘 흘러간다는 뜻이에요. 행사나 회의 이야기에 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means it goes on without problems; common for events and meetings.

phrases.example: 회의가 진행되는 동안 휴대폰을 꺼 주세요.
phrases.en: Please turn off your phone while the meeting is going on.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-는 동안'을 붙여 일이 이어지는 시간을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add -는 동안 to talk about the time while it goes on.

phrases.en: The construction is not going ahead because of the rain.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-지 않다'를 붙여 일이 앞으로 나아가지 않는다고 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add -지 않다 to say the work isn't moving forward.

explain_en: '진행하다' is a person leading something; '진행되다' is an event moving along through its set steps. Use it for things with an order: meetings, events, construction, classes, interviews. '잘 진행되다' and '순조롭게 진행되다' are common pairings.

en: to form; to build; to develop

examples.en: I build good relationships with friends.

examples.ko: 아이들은 어릴 때 성격을 형성하기 시작해요.
examples.en: Children begin to form their personality when they are young.
The clouds gathered and formed a big rain cloud.
It takes time to form good habits.
A price that has formed does not change right away.
There is a small market that the merchants built up.

explain: 시간이 지나면서 조금씩 모양이 만들어지는 것에 써요. 관계, 습관, 성격, 가격처럼 눈에 안 보이는 것에 자주 써요. 물건을 한 번에 만드는 것은 '만들다'를 써요.

phrases.en: Good habits form slowly.
phrases.nuance_ko: 저절로 만들어진다는 느낌이에요. 내가 만들면 '형성하다'예요.
phrases.nuance_en: Gives the sense of forming on its own. When you do it yourself, use '형성하다'.

phrases.en: I want to build a habit of exercising every day.
phrases.nuance_ko: 시간을 들여 습관을 조금씩 만든다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means building a habit little by little over time.

phrases.example: 서로 신뢰를 형성하는 데 시간이 걸려요.
phrases.en: It takes time to build trust with each other.
phrases.nuance_ko: 믿음처럼 눈에 안 보이는 것이 조금씩 생길 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when something invisible like trust develops gradually.

explain_en: It describes something taking shape little by little over time. It is often used for things you cannot see, such as relationships, habits, personality and prices. For making a physical object in one go, use '만들다'.

p.n: 형성시키다 stresses deliberately making it happen.

en: applicant; person who wishes to take part

examples.en: Those who wish to attend, please sign up by Friday.
Only those who want to take part join this volunteer activity.
There were too many people who wanted it, so we decided by lottery.

examples.ko: 희망자에게는 따로 안내 메일을 보내 드려요.
examples.en: We send a separate information email to those who wish.
I gave the teacher the list of people who want to go on the outing.

examples.ko: 해외 연수 희망자를 지금 받고 있어요.
examples.en: We are now accepting people who want to join the overseas training.

explain: '참가 희망자', '입사 희망자'처럼 앞에 활동을 붙여서 많이 써요. '지원자'는 공식적으로 지원한 사람이고, 희망자는 하고 싶다고 한 사람 쪽에 가까워요.

phrases.example: 참가 희망자는 여기에 이름을 써 주세요.
phrases.en: Those who wish to take part, please write your name here.
phrases.nuance_ko: 행사나 대회에 참가하고 싶은 사람을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to people who want to join an event or contest.

phrases.en: Many people want to join the company, so competition is tough.
phrases.nuance_ko: 회사에 들어가고 싶은 사람을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to people who want to get into a company.
phrases.en_equiv: person who wants to join a company

phrases.en: Only those who want to, please sign up for this class.
phrases.nuance_ko: '만'을 붙여 하고 싶은 사람만 대상이라고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 만 means only those who want to are included.

explain_en: It is often used with an activity in front, like '참가 희망자' or '입사 희망자'. '지원자' is someone who formally applied, while 희망자 leans toward someone who said they want to do it.
